name: Cheese pashtida with spinach + whole-spelt pasta — logged batch

source.author: Logged batch — actually cooked 2026-10-24
source.notes: A batch the user actually cooked, logged as a reference per the standing skill. Based on cheese_pashtida_spinach (the adopted spinach-optimized pashtida), with 3 handfuls of whole-spelt pasta added to the batter and baked together, as suggested. TOTAL batch = the full cheese_pashtida_spinach recipe (4 eggs, cottage, white cheese, whole-spelt flour, baking powder, 9% yellow cheese, 180 g feta, cream cheese, 150 g raw spinach, no added salt) PLUS 3 handfuls of whole-spelt pasta. Makes 9 slices (bulkier than the 8-slice base due to the added pasta); macros below are PER SLICE (batch ÷ 9). ASSUMPTIONS (not given — flag and adjust if off): (1) '3 handfuls' taken as ~90 g DRY pasta (~30 g/handful, a standard dry-pasta handful); (2) the pasta was added DRY/uncooked directly into the batter and cooked through in the oven (not pre-boiled) — 'just baked as suggested' read as no extra step beyond the base recipe's bake. Tell me if either assumption is off (exact weight, or if the pasta was pre-cooked) and I'll correct the macros. Estimate.

serving_desc: 1 slice (~180 g baked) — batch makes 9 (bulkier than the base 8-slice pashtida)

ingredients.note: NEW vs the base recipe — amount assumed; added dry/uncooked into the batter

ingredients.qty: none — as in the base recipe

steps: Whisk the eggs; mix in the cottage, white cheese, whole-spelt flour and baking powder.
Fold in the yellow cheese, feta, cream cheese, raw spinach, and the 3 handfuls of dry whole-spelt pasta.
Pour into a greased/lined baking dish and level the top.

Bake at 180 °C, top-bottom heat, until set and golden on top and the pasta is cooked through (likely longer than the base recipe's 35-45 min given the added dry pasta — check doneness by taste/texture of the pasta, not just the custard).

batch_totals.note: Whole bake (9 slices), incl. ~90 g dry whole-spelt pasta (assumed amount — flag if different). Vs cheese_pashtida_spinach (per slice ~127 kcal / 12.5 g protein / 0.7 g fiber): similar protein, meaningfully more carbs and fiber from the pasta (whole-spelt pasta is a real fiber source), slightly lower calcium/sodium per slice since the batch is split 9 ways instead of 8.

him.verdict: Adding whole-spelt pasta turns the egg-cheese pashtida into more of a complete one-dish meal — carbs jump from ~5 g to ~11 g per slice and fiber more than doubles (~1.4 g vs ~0.7 g), while protein stays essentially the same (~12.4 g) and fat barely moves. Protein density drops a little (~8.4 g protein per 100 kcal vs ~9.9 g in the spinach-only version) simply because pasta adds calories without adding protein, but this is now a more balanced, filling dish — good as an actual meal rather than a side. Baking the pasta dry into the batter is a clever no-extra-pot move, assuming it cooked through properly.
flags: ~12.4 g protein / 148 kcal slice (~8.4 g protein per 100 kcal — still strong, slightly diluted by the pasta carbs)
fiber roughly doubled vs the spinach-only version (~1.4 g vs ~0.7 g) — whole-spelt pasta is a real contributor
more balanced as a standalone meal now (protein + carb + veg in one dish)
sodium/calcium per slice ticked down slightly (same batch, split 9 ways instead of 8)
confirm the pasta cooked through — dry pasta baked in a custard can undercook if the batter doesn't release enough moisture
suggested_mods: If the pasta came out undercooked, next time par-boil it 3-4 min first, drain, then fold in — more reliable doneness
This works well as a full meal on its own; the spinach-only version is still the better pick when you want a leaner side
Pair with a simple salad for extra vitamin C/fiber if eating this as the main dish

her_preconception.verdict: Still a strong preconception dish — the folate from the spinach carries over almost unchanged (~44 mcg DFE/slice), and the added whole-spelt pasta brings a bit more fiber and B-vitamins on top. Protein, choline and calcium remain solid. No new safety concerns versus the base recipe (fully baked; verify the feta is pasteurized as before).
prenatal_highlights: folate from spinach carries over (~44 mcg DFE/slice)
added fiber + B-vitamins from whole-spelt pasta
protein, choline, calcium unchanged in substance

safety_advisories.note: Feta is a brined cheese — Listeria risk unless pasteurized. Baked through here (cooked = considered safe); verify pasteurized, same as the base recipe.

suggested_mods: No changes needed — this remains a good folate + protein dish for her, now also more filling as a full meal

cooking_guide: Follow the cheese_pashtida_spinach method (whisk eggs, mix in cottage/white cheese/whole-spelt flour/baking powder, fold in yellow cheese, feta, cream cheese and raw spinach).
Fold in the 3 handfuls of dry whole-spelt pasta last, distributing it evenly through the batter so no pocket of dry pasta is left uncoated.

Pour into a greased/lined dish and level. Because there's now dry pasta that needs to cook through (not just an egg custard to set), give it a bit more time than the base recipe and check the pasta's texture, not just whether the top is golden.
Tip for next time: if any pasta came out chewy/undercooked, par-boiling it 3-4 min first (then draining well) before folding in gives a more reliably cooked result without changing the macros much.
